To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interplay between integrins, the JNK pathway, and PI4P 5-kinase Sktl is crucially important for setting up cell polarity and reepithelisation during Drosophilal wound healing.

Sktl, the enzyme synthesizing the lipid PI(4, 5)P2 in Drosophila, is required for cell polarity and reepithelization during wound healing and its localization at the rear side is interdependent on integrin localization and JNK signaling.
the Sktl localization is crucial for the reepithelialization during Drosophla larval wound healing and the Sktl localization requires the JNK pathway activation.

the molecular mechanisms underlying wound healing and tissue regeneration in Drosophila.
the molecular basis of cell polarization and re-epithelialisation in Drosophila.
understanding how PI(4, 5)P2 regulates cell adhesion to the extracellular matrix and how it is involved in the regulation of the cell polarity during wound closure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the interplay between integrins, JNK and Sktl sets up the polarity of cells in order to allow the epidermal sheet to move forward during wound healing.
Sktl is a crucial regulator of the cell polarization and re-epithelialization of the Drosophilae epidermal sheet during wound healing.

integrin and Sktl are both localized to cell rear during wound healing and that the two proteins are interdependent for cell polarity.
the JNK signalling regulates cell polarity by modulating Sktl and integrin localization during wound healing.

the interplay between PI(4, 5)P2 kinase Sktl and integrin βPS at the rear side is critical for the cell polarity that is crucial for wound closure.
